security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and key-name findings are false positives from Markdown code examples, TypeScript template literals, and redaction lists. The playbook does include real outbound telemetry examples and user-context enrichment, so users should validate endpoints and redact personal data before implementation.

remediation.issue: Outbound telemetry can include stack traces, request data, or user identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Document endpoint allowlisting, provider ownership checks, retention limits, sampling, and redaction before enabling network sends.

remediation.issue: User context enrichment can expose personal data in error events.
remediation.suggestion: Minimize event.user fields, hash stable identifiers where possible, and filter PII before sending events to external services.

remediation.issue: Examples combine production integrations with placeholder configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings that credentials, DSNs, webhook URLs, and alert destinations must come from trusted project configuration.

content.value_statement: Production teams need clear error signals before incidents grow. This skill guides tracking setup, structured logs, alerts, grouping, recovery, and dashboards.
actual_capabilities: Assess current error handling, logging, and monitoring gaps.
Plan Sentry-style and custom error tracking integrations.
Design structured logging with redaction, audit logs, and request logs.
Define alert rules with thresholds, cooldowns, and notification channels.
Plan error grouping, recovery strategies, and monitoring dashboards.
Provide verification checklists and rollout steps.
limitations: Does not operate a monitoring service or store telemetry by itself.
Requires project-specific credentials, endpoints, and privacy rules from the user.
Example code must be adapted and tested in the target stack.
Does not replace incident response ownership or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Add Production Error Tracking
use_cases.description: Create a practical plan for capturing exceptions, context, stack traces, and release data in a service.

use_cases.title: Improve Alert Quality
use_cases.description: Define alert thresholds, cooldowns, routing rules, and dashboards that reduce noise during incidents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Rollout
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable checklist for logging, grouping, privacy controls, and monitoring across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my application error handling approach. Identify logging, alerting, grouping, and monitoring gaps. Give me prioritized next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Structured Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured logging plan for my service. Include log levels, request context, redaction rules, audit events, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Design alert rules for production errors. Include thresholds, cooldowns, severity levels, routing, escalation, and dashboard metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Full Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an end-to-end error diagnostics rollout for my stack. Cover tracking integration, privacy controls, grouping, recovery, dashboards, and launch validation.

output_examples.input: A Node service has uncaught exceptions and noisy logs.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering global handlers, structured logs, redaction, error grouping, alert thresholds, and deployment validation.

output_examples.input: An SRE team wants fewer false positive error alerts.
output_examples.output: Recommended alert rules with severity tiers, cooldown windows, routing guidance, dashboard metrics, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A team needs a monitoring dashboard for recent production errors.
output_examples.output: Dashboard sections for error rate, affected users, top errors, active alerts, recent events, and recovery progress.

best_practices: Define privacy and redaction rules before sending error events to any provider.
Group related errors so alerts represent incidents, not repeated stack traces.
Validate alerts with test incidents before relying on them in production.
anti_patterns: Forwarding full request payloads, cookies, or tokens into error telemetry.
Alerting on every exception without thresholds, sampling, or cooldowns.
Adding dashboards without assigning owners for triage and response.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design error tracking, structured logging, alerts, grouping, recovery workflows, and monitoring dashboards.

faq.question: Does it require a specific provider?
faq.answer: No. It includes patterns for common providers and custom tracking, but users choose the final tools.

faq.question: Can it write production-ready code?
faq.answer: It can draft implementation guidance and examples. Teams must adapt, test, and review code in their own environment.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Use explicit redaction, minimize user context, validate endpoints, and avoid sending secrets or full request payloads.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, SRE teams, DevOps engineers, and engineering leads improving production reliability.

faq.question: Does it replace incident response tooling?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan diagnostics and monitoring, but teams still need operational ownership and response processes.
